title: A household thermometer or a weather app with a grown-up (written guide in the pupil PDF)
subject: Computing
unit: Spring 1: Repetition in shapes and data logging
source: Seeded from computing/y4 lesson 9 (A household thermometer or a weather app with a grown-up (written guide in the pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 9: Data logging: planning a temperature log. A practical to do at home with an adult nearby. Read it all first.

practical.aim: To understand how a data log records measurements at regular intervals
equipment: Tarbiyyah Primary computing long-term plan 2023-24, Year 4 Spring 1 (Repetition in Shapes; Data Logging), built on the NCCE Teach Computing Curriculum
safety: Written guide in the pupil PDF
An adult knows what you are doing and is nearby
Clear a space and tidy up afterwards; wash your hands
method: From the table, when was the kitchen warmest?
How much did it warm up between 8:00 and 12:00?
What is the interval in the table?
Core: Plan your own temperature log at home: one room, 5 times, equal intervals. Fill the time and place columns.
Extend: Predict when your room will be warmest and why. Write in the portal response box. Start: 'I predict...'
Stretch: Explain why taking readings 'whenever I remember' would not be fair.

questions.q: A data log records... A) one reading B) readings over time C) a password
Core: Plan your own temperature log at home: one room, 5 times, equal intervals. Fill the time and place columns.
questions.model: Teacher fills the first two rows of the plan for the kitchen at 2-hour intervals.

questions.q: Extend: Predict when your room will be warmest and why. Write in the portal response box. Start: 'I predict...'
questions.a: For example: I predict 13:00, because the sun shines in and the heating has been on.
